# Dual-build Rust device test whose Bazel test packaging is blocked by a Bazel analysis failure outside the change (e.g. duplicate dylib in package runfiles), while the GN copy generated by bazel2gn is packaged by a hand-written GN test package above the sentinel

- **Learned from:** inner loop friction on a local task (task `starnix-block-server`)
- **Date:** 2026-10-22
- **Changed:** `checks/cq_reachability.sh`, `checks/manifest.json`, `checks/migration_sanity.sh`

## Root cause

migration_sanity/rust_unit_test_layout and
cq_reachability/unpackaged_rust_device_test required a Bazel fx_unittest_package
or fx_packaged_binary for every device rustc_test, with no way to record that
Bazel packaging fails analysis for reasons the coder may not fix (shared rule or
dylib runfiles duplication). coder.md already allows keeping a test GN-only when
Bazel cannot express it, but the checks contradicted that, so the coder got
stuck disputing ERRORs that could never be cleared.

## Why not a one-off fix

Any Rust library whose test transitively reaches a rustc_dylib through two paths
hits the same duplicate-.so packaging failure. Without a deterministic,
documented escape (marker comment plus verified hand-written GN package wrapping
the generated test), every such migration loops on unfixable ERRORs or is pushed
into editing shared Bazel rules. Fixing one directory's BUILD files does not
change that.
